comment: I'd always heard good things about him, but I didn't think it was possible for anyone to warrant such high praise. Shugrue made me fall in love with chemistry. He's so clearly passionate about the content he's teaching, and he's genuinely excited for you to find your own niche, too. He rewards the effort when you put in the time.

Love Dr. Shugrue, literally the best professor I've ever taken. I would take him for any classes he teaches. As long as you actually study the material and listen to lectures, you can easily get an A. Also just an amazing and caring person, and always tries to understand your situation and workload.

Orgo 2 is notoriously difficult, but Dr. Shugrue has amazing lectures. He truly cares and is very responsive. His grading was fair, and there was 1 or 2 points of extra credit for every exam. Overall, I loved the class, but my grade was not handed to me; you have to work very hard to get an A. On a day-to-day basis, class is not that much work :)

Easily the best professor I've had at UR; really funny and engaging lecturer, with an impressive knowledge of drug design that's parsed in an easy to understand way. Loved the presentation-based focus of class and the open-ended final research project. Homework/quizzes were challenging but very fair, I'd take this class 7 days a week if I could.

I had Dr. Shugrue for orgo 1 and 2. He was an excellent professor. His mannerisms could be a little awkward at times, but he was always so sweet and caring. He wanted to make sure that his students were getting the most out of his lectures. My only regret from that class was not utilizing his office hours.

I had Shugrue for both 205 and 206, and he changed a lot. This semester he suddenly became a really harsh grader, and honestly was not very nice anymore. I still liked his lectures and the way he structured the class, but he started taking tons of points off on exams for tiny mistakes, and my exam grade was wayy lower than it should've been.

He is not very accessible outside of the classroom. I asked for help and was told to just read the textbook again. Unless you are comfortable teaching yourself, he is not the best prof to take. All material is cumulative so if you don't get one thing, it's difficult.

Orgo is a difficult class but Dr Shugrue does a good job of making it manageable. Lectures are fast paced but it is clear what he wants you to know. He does not assign much homework. Tests are very difficult but he gives lots of partial credit. He is a tough but fair grader. Be prepared to spend hours studying and go to office hours.

Dr.Shugrue is a good professor overall, Orgo is just difficult. He goes over concepts too quickly sometimes and before you know it, you go from memorizing 4 mechanisms for exam 2 to 15 mechanisms for exam 3. My advice is to get a tutor from early in the semester! Do not overload your schedule bc you'll need to focus and practice practice practice

Dr. Shugrue is one of the best ever! He cares about his students a lot and is very open to meet with students outside of class. His class is very structured and is clear on what to expect grading wise. I recommend him!!!

Great professor. It's clear that he really wants his students to do well and understand the material as well as why it's important. He was really receptive to student feedback and was very accessible outside of class. Even if orgo isn't your best subject, he makes it as easy to understand as possible.

Shugrue is great. The class is fast-paced, but that's just bc Orgo has a ton of material. Shugrue handles it well to make sure everyone feels good with the material while also not falling behind schedule. Pretty sure all of the orgo profs here are great though, so don't stress it. I'm staying with Shugrue for 206 bc his style meshes well with me.

Shugrue is a G. Easy tests because he gives you 2 practice tests before every exam. Material and concepts might be hard at first sometimes, but he gives so many practice problems that it becomes easy. Nothing that he doesn't teach is tested. Textbook is "required" but I never read anything and did none of the practice. Makes orgo an easy A.

Amazing professor, amazing class. Dr. Shugrue put so much effort into teaching/developing the class and was receptive to student feedback. I went to him several times for office hours and he was always available- he even stayed late one time. The class itself was very organic synthesis-heavy, but I learned a lot and really liked the course format.
If you are an Organic Chemistry fan, then I highly recommend that you take his CHEM 433 course. It is really a great class, and I learned a lot from him.

One of the best professors at UR. His lectures are excellent! He knows how to explain complex concepts and ensures the students know why the concepts matter. He's also clear about his expectations for students. He is very organized, understanding, kind, and patient. 10000000/10

Amazing professor. He made a subject that I thought would be very difficult into one of my favorites! He's always accessible outside of class and very transparent with grading. Offers great feedback and lots of practice problems to help with studying!

Great professor. He is very clear with what he will put on exams, and he provides useful studying materials. He is very accessible outside of class and excited to answer any questions. He lectures and goes through material very quickly, but as long as you complete the problem sets, practice questions, and practice exams you'll be fine.
CHEM 206 Lecture: Good Prof. New, and a lover of graduate school stories

LAB: This was his first semester teaching, and was a good lab professor. He wanted his students to succeed and gave the opportunity to submit late work before the end of the semester. He's very easy to reach outside of class, email and in-person, and was very approachable and helpful. He's a generous grader, who gives good feedback on work.
